newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission sees legal risk in German car plan.
newsitem.headline: Commission sees legal risk in German car plan.

text.p: The European Commission decided on Wednesday to send a letter to Germany pointing out possible legal risks in a plan for fiscal incentives to encourage the purchase of cars meeting stricter environmental standards.

An official said the Commission was satisfied that a German plan was based on the proposed Auto/Oil programme, COM(96)248, a package of standards for fuel quality and limits on car exhaust gases intended to slash road transport emissions by up to 70 percent by the year 2010.

But since that programme was only a proposal and may be changed by the European Parliament and by Council, using it as a baseline for the planned incentive scheme could nevertheless pose legal problems.
"There is a risk that parliament and Council are going to change our proposal," he said. "So there is a risk for them."
Germany wants to give fiscal incentives for those cars which respect already in 1997 or 1998 the values for engine emissions which will are to be binding from 2000/2001.
Bonn had asked the Commission for its opinion on the issue. The letter had not been finalised yet but would probably be sent in the next few days.

Environment ministers gave their first response to the proposed Auto/Oil measures earlier this month while parliament awaits its first official treatment of the dossier in a puiblic hearing on November 20.
Commission official Richard Wright estimated early this year that final adoption of the overall package might not come before June 1998.
